name: Developer guide
intro: Use Babbage's calculation engine in your own Rust program. It is the crate babbage-core: give it a line of plain language and it hands back an exact value. Every code sample in this guide is compiled and run by the project's tests.

chapters.title: Getting started
chapters.description: Add the crate, evaluate a line, show the answer.

chapters.title: Evaluating lines
chapters.description: Values, kinds, units, and what a line can be.

chapters.title: Showing answers
chapters.description: Decimal places, number formats, repeating decimals and the exact flag.

chapters.title: Sheets
chapters.description: Lines that use the lines above them: names, references, tags and totals.

chapters.title: Settings and time
chapters.description: Clocks, time zones, tax, regional dollars and holidays.

chapters.title: Errors and guarantees
chapters.description: What can fail, what stays exact, and what 1.x promises.

chapters.title: Recipes
chapters.description: A command-line calculator, a one-call helper and inline answers in text.
